subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Should #91839 remain the cross-surface tracker for the provider model-unavailable plus subagent announce plus gateway starvation incident, and what owner boundary should own the permanent bounded-failure behavior?
rationale: The safe fix crosses provider error semantics, subagent completion delivery, config reload validation, and gateway availability; automation cannot choose whether to solve that as one incident, split it across existing issues, or intentionally treat the config edit as operator fault.

options.title: Keep the cross-surface tracker
options.body: Use #91839 to coordinate the bounded runtime failure design, with #90178, #84212, and #91307 linked as partial implementation or validation tracks.

options.title: Fold into existing issues after proof
options.body: Close #91839 only after live proof shows #90178, #84212, and #91307 jointly cover the exact provider-error storm without leaving a combined gap.

options.title: Treat as operator config fault
options.body: Document the bad-model edit as unsupported and accept that runtime recovery remains bounded only by existing generic mechanisms.

recommendation.title: Keep the cross-surface tracker
recommendation.body: Use #91839 to coordinate the bounded runtime failure design, with #90178, #84212, and #91307 linked as partial implementation or validation tracks.

likelyOwner.reason: The subagent lifecycle/retry boundary is the central coordination point, and Peter Steinberger has recent history on that path.
